- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.00) in last 3–5 days, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >72.00, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67), model often lags 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- If 30d forecast is >73.00 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is >10% below forecast, check sentiment history for recent negative signals; adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% per day.
